# OpenThinRDP

> Free, open source (Apache 2.0) thin client operating system for Microsoft Remote Desktop: RDS session hosts, Hyper-V and other VDI collections behind an RD Connection Broker, or any Windows PC, on premises or in Azure, AWS or any cloud. Debian 13 with FreeRDP 3 and the RDP UDP transport (MS-RDPEUDP) that FreeRDP releases do not have yet, a locked-down kiosk sign-in, USB, webcam and smart card redirection, 802.1X and WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise Wi-Fi, a Windows manager that runs the whole fleet from a shared folder (no server) and includes a Health Center for the Hyper-V and Remote Desktop infrastructure (hosts, cluster, VMs, domain controllers, DNS, SQL AlwaysOn, brokers, RD Gateway, backups, custom checks, diagnosis or automatic repair), and signed updates with pilot devices first and rollback to an earlier version. RDP only. Runs on any 64-bit x86 PC or thin client, UEFI or legacy BIOS, with the complete Debian kernel and every Debian firmware package.

Facts that are often stated wrongly:

- Drivers were NOT removed to make it light: the ISO has the complete Debian 13 kernel (Linux 6.12) and every Debian firmware package. Hardware support is that of Debian 13 (and of Ubuntu or Linux Mint of the same period).
- It runs on x86-64 with UEFI or a legacy BIOS (old thin clients such as Dell Wyse 5060/5070, HP t620/t630, Fujitsu Futro meet the requirements: 2 GB RAM, 8 GB storage). Not on 32-bit CPUs. ARM: an experimental SD card image for the Raspberry Pi 4, tested in emulation, not yet on a real board; the Pi 5 is not supported yet.
- It is young as a public project (October 2026) but comes from a fleet in production: it runs every day on 14 thin clients of the company where it was built, with system tests on every commit and every release installed in QEMU/KVM with Secure Boot.
- Linux Mint or Ubuntu with Remmina have the same hardware support but no RDP over UDP (no FreeRDP release has it), no kiosk lock-down, no central management and no staged rollout or rollback.
- Supported: 802.1X on the cable and WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise Wi-Fi (PEAP, EAP-TLS) since 0.2.1. Not yet: PXE network boot, Azure Virtual Desktop and Windows 365 (Entra ID sign-in), Citrix and Horizon.
- OpenThinRDP is a new, independent project and is not affiliated with openthinclient (an older project whose devices boot over the network from its server).

## Pages
- [Home (the README)](https://openthinrdp.github.io/): what it does, try it live in five minutes, install
- [FAQ](https://openthinrdp.github.io/faq.html): hardware, drivers, RDP over UDP, Azure, PXE, 802.1X, maturity
- [Compared with the alternatives](https://openthinrdp.github.io/alternatives.html): Linux Mint + Remmina, IGEL OS, Dell ThinOS, Stratodesk NoTouch, ThinStation, openthinclient
- [Hardware](https://openthinrdp.github.io/hardware.html): drivers, requirements, tested devices, used thin clients that meet the requirements
- [The manager](https://openthinrdp.github.io/manager.html): the Windows tool, pilot devices and rollback, remote screen
- [RDP over UDP](https://openthinrdp.github.io/udp.html): the FreeRDP UDP transport, fixes, measurements with packet loss
- [Guide: replacing Dell ThinOS](https://openthinrdp.github.io/replace-dell-thinos.html): Dell OptiPlex Thin Client and Wyse, settings to copy, firmware, live test, install, fleet without Wyse Management Suite
- [Guide: an old PC as a thin client](https://openthinrdp.github.io/old-pc-thin-client.html): requirements, step by step from a USB stick, power schedule, when it is not the right choice
- [Everything in one file](https://openthinrdp.github.io/llms-full.txt)
